newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia Airlines buys Airbus to boost Euro traffic.
newsitem.headline: Croatia Airlines buys Airbus to boost Euro traffic.

text.p: Croatia Airlines' decision to buy planes from Europe's Airbus rather than American Boeing was motivated by aircraft size and plans to boost its buisness within Europe, its president said on Wednesday.
"Choosing Airbus, we are targeting the countries of the consortium -- Germany, France and Great Britain -- which are our main markets in Europe," Matija Katicic told reporters.
He said it hoped their governments would soon approve more frequent flights on the current routes and new ones to other destinations from various Croatian airports.
The airline already flies between the main cities in Europe and Croatian capital Zagreb. Some routes, like London, Frankfurt and Zurich, are flown on a daily basis.
The company announced its decision on the aircraft supplier last Friday. But Katicic said it has yet to decide on who to buy new engines from.
He confirmed both Airbus and Boeing had offered excellent technology and similar terms for its purchase, which will run well into the next century. All aspects were carefully weighed.
Although they will require more pilot training than the equivalent Boeing, the Airbus A-319s, representing the bulk of new planes, have been chosen because they have a wider body.
"These seven inches offer better comfort to passengers and the possibility to load a lot more cargo," Katicic added.
In a bid to gradually replace and expand its fleet, the airline plans to buy a total of between 14 and 16 medium-range planes and another 2-3 long-range ones later.
Its five Boeing 737-200s are already 15 years old.
Croatia Airlines is also looking at adding another four short-range planes to its current fleet of three ATR-42s and swap them out over time. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
